title: The Internet once switched protocols on a deadline
body: On 1 January 1983 ARPANET turned off its old NCP protocol and required TCP/IP, a coordinated 'flag day' planned in RFC 801. A few dozen hosts could be migrated by decree. The modern Internet, with billions of devices, could never cut over that way, which is why IPv6 instead coexists with IPv4 indefinitely.
source_hint: RFC 801, NCP to TCP transition plan (1981)
